html:
A sports club in Cairo, founded in 1907, whose football team is the most successful in Africa. Its name means "the national".

Egypt was under British occupation, and Al Ahly was founded as a club for Egyptians at a time when many clubs were for foreigners. That gave it a nationalist flavour from the start. Its great rival is Zamalek, founded in 1911, and the Cairo derby between them divides the city.

Football became Egypt's mass passion in the 20th century. Egypt was the first African country to play at a World Cup, in 1934. Al Ahly has won the Egyptian league far more often than any other club and holds the record number of African Champions League titles.

Its fans also played a part in politics. Al Ahly's ultras fought police in Tahrir Square during the Arab Spring uprising of 2011. In February 2012, 72 Ahly fans were killed after a match in Port Said, the worst disaster in Egyptian sport.
sum: A sports club in Cairo, founded in 1907, whose football team is the most successful in Africa. Its name means "the national".
